title.narrative: Improving experiences of severe stigmatising skin diseases in Ghana and Ethiopia

description.narrative: Recruitment of patients into the trial based on both active and passive case search activities to allow enough time for case follow-up. SHARP Objectives specific to Noguchi include 1. To evaluate integrated community-based strategies for early diagnosis, adherence support and stigma reduction. 2. To undertake facility-based trials of dressings for Buruli Ulcer. 3. To promote collaboration and build research capacity in Ghana and Ethiopia.

The Skin Health Africa Research Programme (SHARP) aims to improve outcomes for people with severe stigmatising skin diseases (SSSDs) in Ghana and Ethiopia by strengthening the care cascade through scalable strategies for earlier detection, improving management to reduce disability and counteracting stigma and discrimination. SHARP is a collaboration between the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) in the UK, the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research, University of Ghana (NMIMR UG) and the Kumasi Centre for Collaborative Research in Tropical Medicine of Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KCCR, KNUST) in Ghana, and the Armauer Hansen Research Institute (AHRI) and Addis Ababa University (AAU) in Ethiopia Training activities related to the implementation of a health facility-based skin health intervention as well as a community based to equip the health workers to effectively implement the skin Health intervention in their respective health facilities was conducted. Staff from all 17 health facilities in the Atwima Mponua District were involved in the trainings which adopted a two- step approach: first a trainer of trainersâ€™ session was held for all health facility in-charges endline survey. Availability of the trained personnel facilitated our implementation of both the health facility-based skin health intervention as well as the community-based endline survey of the project. To create community awareness about our skin health intervention, various community engagement activities were conducted. This included: a. Community Durbars b. Radio/community announcements c. Project information dissemination during Antenatal (ANC) and child welfare clinics (CWC) Community members were notified of the availability of our skin health intervention in their district to inform their health seeking decision making. Medicines, wound tracker logbooks, wound care packs, point of care diagnostics kits for yaws, as well as sample collection kits for Buruli ulcer and yaws samples were provided to all health facilities in the district. Supplies needed to take care of patients with skin conditions were available at the various health facilities to support the implementation of the skin health intervention.
